newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs extend gains, others mixed.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs extend gains, others mixed.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Wednesday with Brent crude CFDs and naphtha narrowly firmer, low sulphur fuel and gasoline a touch easier.

Brent CFDs marginally extended gains made late Tuesday on the back of a physical deal. The balance of this week was pegged around July -12.5 cents against July compared with 13/14 cents below yesterday, while next week was also at -12.5 cents compared with -15 cents.
Further out values were also stronger with June 2-6 assessed around 15 cents under July from -18/19 cents with June 9-13 ratcheting up to 17 cents under from 20 cents.
Heavy fuel swaps were broadly steady with June talked around $84-85 a tonne with physical trading at $83.25 and $83.50 for prompt with later material closer to June swaps.

Low sulphur cargo swaps were a touch weaker after the $98 heard done on June on Tuesday. Dealers said June was up to $1.50 below this, but that contango into July remained. Physical near-term barrels were not being shown.
Gasoline swaps had yet to get into their stride, but were up to $1.00 a tonne easier with June around $208, July $202 and Augusta further $2.50 lower.
Naphtha was also slow, but showed modest gains of 50 cents or so with June around $191.50.
